exposure: Ability to pay for doula care
cohort: The study participants were 176 patients, aged 18 to 49 years, who had previous pregnancies, were currently pregnant, were thinking about becoming pregnant, or were not currently considering pregnancy, recruited from two large academic hospitals in South Florida.
finding: Patients with an annual household income between $25,000 and $50,000 were almost five times more likely to express interest in doula care, and among those interested, a statistically significant association existed between the ability to pay for doula care and race.
cross-section timing: Survey data was collected at the time of administration from patients with varying pregnancy statuses.
